patients.summary: Retired Holyoke man with CAD (2020 MI, LAD stent), angina, hypertension and hyperlipidemia who joins in 2021. A severe depressive episode in 2023 answers to mirtazapine; from 2024 a run of cardiology events follows: Mobitz I, a contrast reaction, nifedipine edema, complete heart block with NSTEMI and a pacemaker, VT with an ICD upgrade, a retroperitoneal hematoma after a catheterization, and a bleeding duodenal ulcer.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mr. Pelletier called asking to join the practice. Says his old doctor is cutting back and his daughter heard good things about us. Medicare, retired, lives in Holyoke. Has a cardiologist he sees once a year and wants to keep. Explained membership and how texting the doctor works; he laughed and said his daughter will have to show him. Records release signed over email. Requested records from prior primary care office. New patient visit booked 9/14 at 9:00. Asked him to bring all pill bottles.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: prior primary care
documents.body:
Summary of care, faxed at the patient's request. 38 pages received; key items abstracted below by MA.

Problems: Coronary artery disease. Myocardial infarction February 2020, treated at a regional hospital with a drug-eluting stent to the LAD. Stable angina since. Hypertension. Hyperlipidemia. Osteoarthritis, knees. Former smoker.

Medications at last visit (06/2021): aspirin 81 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg at bedtime; metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg daily; lisinopril 20 mg daily; acetaminophen 500 mg every 6 hours as needed for knee pain.

Allergies: NKDA.

Health maintenance: colonoscopy 2018, normal, no polyps. Pneumococcal: PPSV23 not documented. Influenza yearly. COVID-19 primary series per patient spring 2021 at a pharmacy.

Last labs 06/2021: lipid panel and BMP in normal range per their flowsheet (values not transmitted).

Cardiology: followed yearly by an outside cardiology group since the 2020 MI. Hospital discharge summary from 02/2020 not included in packet.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

Paul is a 68 y/o retired man joining us from another primary care office. Brought every bottle in a grocery bag as asked.

Cardiac history: MI in Feb 2020, taken to the cath lab at a regional hospital, one drug-eluting stent to the LAD. Since then he gets a pressure in the middle of his chest a few times a month, walking up the hill on his street with the dog or carrying bags of mulch. Stops, it goes away in a couple of minutes. Pattern unchanged over the last year. No rest pain, no syncope, no palpitations, no orthopnea. Sees outside cardiology yearly; last there this spring.

Other: BP treated for close to ten years. Cholesterol on atorvastatin since around the same time. Knees ache after gardening, both sides, worse on stairs; acetaminophen a couple of times a week does the job. Never had injections.

Meds (bottles reviewed): aspirin 81 daily, atorvastatin 40 qhs, metoprolol succinate 50 daily, lisinopril 20 daily, acetaminophen 500 q6h prn. Takes them all; uses a weekly pill box.
Allergies: NKDA.

PMH/PSH: as above. Colonoscopy 2018 normal per outside records.
FH: father MI at 62. Mother had high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes. Brother has coronary disease.
SH: retired, divorced, lives alone with his dog; daughter lives nearby and checks in. Smoked about a pack a day for 25 years, quit 2015. Alcohol 1-2 drinks a week, usually beer with the football game. Walks the dog every morning, big vegetable garden.

ROS: no weight change, no GI bleeding, no urinary trouble, mood good. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: Well appearing, pleasant. BP 134/82, HR 62. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. No JVD. Abdomen soft, no bruit, no pulsatile mass. Extremities without edema, pedal pulses 2+. Knees with bony enlargement and crepitus bilaterally, no effusion, full extension. Neuro grossly intact.

A/P:
1. CAD s/p MI and LAD stent 2020, chronic stable angina: symptoms stable and infrequent. Continue aspirin, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol. Will get last cardiology note.
2. HTN: at goal-ish today, continue lisinopril 20. BMP today.
3. Hyperlipidemia: lipid panel today on atorvastatin 40.
4. OA knees: acetaminophen prn, fine as is.
5. Former smoker, 25 pk-yr, quit 6 yrs ago: discussed lung cancer screening, he'd like to do it. Low-dose CT ordered. One-time aortic ultrasound ordered.
6. Health maintenance: PCV20 today. Hep C screen with labs. A1c (mother with DM). Flu shot next month when the high-dose arrives. Colonoscopy UTD (2018).

RTC 4 months, sooner prn.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Paul, your labs from Tuesday look good. Kidney function, potassium and liver tests are normal, blood count normal, A1c is in the normal range so no sign of diabetes, and the hepatitis C screen is negative. LDL cholesterol on the atorvastatin is close to what your old office had. The CT scheduling office will call you about the lung scan and the aorta ultrasound. Nice to have you with us.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for flu and COVID booster. Afebrile. Screening questions negative, no prior vaccine reactions. High-dose flu 0.7 mL IM left deltoid. Pfizer COVID booster 0.3 mL IM right deltoid. VIS and EUA fact sheet given. Waited 15 minutes, no issues. Vaccine card updated.

events.reason: Lung cancer screening and aortic screening

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING (BASELINE)
Indication: 68-year-old former smoker, 25 pack-years, quit 2015.
Technique: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without IV contrast.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Lungs: No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or emphysema. Airways patent. Pleura: No effusion or thickening. Mediastinum: No lymphadenopathy. Heart normal in size. Coronary artery calcification, with a stent in the left anterior descending artery. Thoracic aorta normal in caliber. Upper abdomen: unremarkable. Bones: degenerative change in the thoracic spine.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening with low-dose CT in 12 months. Coronary artery calcification and LAD stent noted.

reports.text:
ULTRASOUND ABDOMINAL AORTA, SCREENING
Indication: Male, former smoker, age 68.
Findings: The abdominal aorta is visualized from the diaphragm to the bifurcation. Normal caliber throughout, measured in the anteroposterior plane. No aneurysm or dissection flap. Common iliac arteries normal in caliber.
reports.conclusion: Normal caliber abdominal aorta. No abdominal aortic aneurysm.

documents.title: CT and ultrasound results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Paul, the lung screening CT was clear, no nodules. It does show calcium in the heart arteries and your stent, which we already knew about. The ultrasound of your aorta was normal, no aneurysm, and that one never needs repeating. Next lung CT in a year; we will send a reminder.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 4 month check. Doing fine through the holidays. Chest pressure maybe twice in December shoveling, both times eased within a few minutes of stopping. No rest symptoms. Taking meds. Knees stiff in the cold.
O: Vitals reviewed, BP in range. Heart RRR, lungs clear, no edema.
A/P: HTN controlled on lisinopril 20 / metoprolol 50; BMP today. Stable angina, unchanged pattern, continue regimen; cardiology yearly in Feb. OA knees stable. RTC 5 months.

documents.title: Cardiology annual follow-up letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group. Date of visit 02/02/2022.

Dear colleague,
I saw Mr. Pelletier for his yearly visit. He is two years out from his MI treated with a drug-eluting stent to the LAD. He has infrequent exertional chest pressure, unchanged, relieved promptly by rest. No dyspnea, presyncope or palpitations.
Medications: aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, acetaminophen as needed.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Exam: blood pressure at goal, pulse regular. JVP normal. Clear lungs. No murmur. No edema.
ECG: sinus rhythm, normal intervals.
Impression: CAD s/p LAD stent, chronic stable angina with low symptom burden, hypertension and hyperlipidemia controlled.
Plan: continue current medicines. See back in a year, sooner with any change in his pattern.
Thank you for allowing me to share in his care.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Garden season. Knees sore after a day of weeding, left a bit more than right, better the next morning. Tylenol 500 once or twice on those days. No locking, no giving way, no swelling. Chest pressure unchanged, rare. Mood good.

Exam: BP ok. Knees: crepitus both, no effusion, stable ligaments, full ROM with end-range discomfort. Gait normal.

OA knees, mild and stable. Talked about kneeling pad, a garden stool, keeping up the walking. Can use acetaminophen up to 3 g a day; stay away from ibuprofen/naproxen with his aspirin and heart history. Does not know when his last tetanus shot was and is in the dirt all summer: Tdap today. HTN fine. Physical in September.

documents.title: Missed visit follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt missed 9:30 BP check. Called him; he forgot, was at his daughter's helping with a fence. Feels fine. Since physical is next month he'd rather fold it into that. OK per PCP. Confirmed 9/20.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
MEDICARE AWV (subsequent)

Health risk assessment reviewed with patient. Lives alone with his dog in a single-family house, no stairs to the bedroom. Independent with all daily activities, drives, cooks, does his own shopping. No falls in the past year. Hearing fine per patient; wears readers. Sleep 7 hours. Diet: lots of vegetables from the garden in summer, more takeout in winter. Activity: dog walks twice daily, about 30 min each.

PHQ-9: 2. Cognition: 3-word recall 3/3, clock normal.

Current problems: CAD s/p LAD stent 2020, stable angina, HTN, hyperlipidemia, OA knees, former smoker.
Meds unchanged. NKDA.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Alert, well. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Skin: no concerning lesions on back or arms.

Prevention:
- Colon: colonoscopy 2018 normal, next due 2028.
- Lung: LDCT 10/2021 Lung-RADS 1, repeat due next month, ordered.
- AAA: screened 2021, normal.
- Vaccines: PCV20 done 2021, Tdap 6/2022. Shingrix #1 today, #2 in 2-6 months (pharmacy is fine). Flu and the new bivalent COVID booster next month.
- Advance directive: he has a health care proxy naming his daughter; copy requested.

Labs today: CMP, lipids, CBC, A1c.
RTC 4 months.

documents.body: Paul, all of your labs from the physical are in a good range. Kidneys, liver, blood count and sugar normal, cholesterol about the same as last year. Nothing to change. Your arm may still be sore from the shingles shot; that usually settles in a day or two.
